Let \(Q(x)=x^2+ax+4\). Since \(1\) is always in \(A\), consider the real roots of \(Q\).

- If \(Q\) has no real roots, \(A=\{1\}\), sum \(1\neq 3\).
- If \(Q\) has a double root \(r\), then \(A=\{1,r\}\).  
  Sum \(=3\Rightarrow r=2\). Thus \(Q(x)=(x-2)^2=x^2-4x+4\), so \(a=-4\).
- If \(Q\) has two distinct real roots \(r_1,r_2\):
  - If one root is \(1\), then \(Q(1)=0\Rightarrow a=-5\), giving roots \(1,4\), so \(A=\{1,4\}\), sum \(5\neq 3\).
  - Otherwise \(A=\{1,r_1,r_2\}\), so \(1+r_1+r_2=3\). Since \(r_1+r_2=-a\), we get \(1-a=3\Rightarrow a=-2\), but then discriminant \(a^2-16=-12<0\), impossible.

Therefore, the only valid value is \(\boxed{-4}\).
